background.definition: Ankylosing spondylitis is a rheumatic disease characterized by chronic low back pain due to sacroiliitis. It is frequently associated with peripheral arthritis, enthesitis, and acute anterior uveitis.

list.listitem: In the United States, the annual age- and sex-adjusted incidence is 7.3 per 100,000 person-years (95% CI, 6.1-8.4).
The estimated prevalence is 0.2% to 1.2%. .
Worldwide prevelance is 0.1% to 1.4% and it is more commom in Europe and Asia. Male to female ratio is 2:1.
The prevalence of ankylosing spondylitis among adults with chronic low back pain is about 5%.
A prospective longitudinal study of 241 patients with ankylosing spondylitis showed an average annual productivity cost of $4945 per patient.

The etiology of ankylosing spondylitis is poorly understood. Immune-mediated mechanisms are suggested by inflammatory histology, raised serum levels of IgA and acute phase reactants, and the close relationship between HLA-B27 and ankylosing spondylitis.
Enthesitis, defined as the inflammatory changes of an enthesis, is the characteristic finding in ankylosing spondylitis.
The enthesis is the insertion of a tendon, ligament, or fascia into bone.
Symptoms suggesting inflammatory back pain include: onset before age 40, insidious onset, persistence of pain for at least 3 months, morning stiffness, and improvement with exercise. C
Radiographic sacroiliitis confirms the diagnosis; however, these findings are often absent during the early years of disease. C
In the presence of inflammatory back pain and negative x-rays, order HLA-B27 to increase the probability of early diagnosis. C

Differential.Differential_Features: Predominantly affects peripheral joints and is rheumatoid factor positive
Usually with characteristic skin and nail disease
Follows a genitourinary or intestinal infection

list.listitem: The most commonly used criteria are the modified New York criteria for the classification of ankylosing spondylitis.
Using these criteria, a patient is diagnosed with ankylosing spondylitis if one clinical criterion is met plus an x-ray showing sacroiliitis.
The clinical criteria consist of inflammatory back pain, limitation of mobility of the lumbar spine, and limitation of chest expansion.
These criteria yield low sensitivity in early disease, as x-ray findings take years to develop.

In a small study, frequency of positive CD 74 antibody was high in both early and late axSpA. Based on sensitivity 80% and specificity of 87% of Anti CD 74 IgG Antibody positivity in active disease, it may be a promising tool to support the clinical diagnosis of Axial Spondyloarthropathy axSpa.
Ankylosing spondylitis usually presents in the third decade of life with chronic low back pain, morning stiffness, and back pain that improves with exercise.

For patients younger than 50 years and back pain longer than 3 months, a clinical decision rule that assesses a combination of stiffness and back pain characteristics can help to determine the probability of ankylosing spondylitis before additional tests are ordered.
Physical examination shows decreased spinal mobility and restricted chest expansion; however, these are late findings and may not be helpful for making an early diagnosis.
In addition to back pain, asymmetric peripheral arthritis, usually of the lower extremities, and acute anterior uveitis may be present.
Aortic insufficiency is a less common finding.
Inflammatory back pain should be evaluated with an x-ray. An x-ray showing sacroiliitis along with clinical criteria defines ankylosing spondylitis.
Unfortunately, it takes years from the onset of clinical symptoms until the appearance of radiographic sacroiliitis; relying on x-ray findings will miss early disease.

HLA-B27 has a strong association with ankylosing spondylitis. The HLA-B27 gene is present in 90% to 95% of white patients with the disease in North America and Europe. HLA-B27 is the laboratory test that best supports the diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis.

MRI shows inflammation in the sacroiliac joints and spine prior to the presence of radiographic sacroiliitis. This may help in earlier diagnosis. More study is needed to define the sensitivity and specificity of MRI.

Under investigation are biomarkers like MMP3, VEGF, calprotectin,leptin,hmw adiponectin,N-telopeptide, procollagen type II and serum amyloid. They have shown some potential for predicting disease progression.

Serum anti-CD74 IgA is a potentially useful diagnostic biomarker for axSpA. However, antibody levels do not correlate with any phenotypical feature, including microscopic gut inflammation, suggesting this to be a disease-specific rather than an inflammatory marker.
See diagnostic algorithm in .
Use NSAIDs A and therapeutic exercises B as first-line therapy, as they improve symptoms and function.
TNF inhibitors (also called anti-TNFs) provide rapid and effective improvement in pain and function; consider their use if NSAIDs and physical therapy are not effective. A

Anti-TNF treatments are associated with more adverse events (but not serious adverse events), including increased susceptibility for injection-site reactions, new infections, or reactivation of latent infections like TB and Hepatitis B. A
Monoclonal antibodies like upadacitinib and ixekizumab have also been shown to be effective in randomized trials. B
Total hip arthroplasty and spinal surgery may be considered for selected patients. C
For many years NSAIDs and therapeutic exercises have been the treatment. NSAIDs have been shown in a 6-week RCT to improve spinal pain, joint pain, and function.
A Cochrane review found low to moderate quality evidence that therapeutic exercises reduce pain, improve function, and decrease patient-assessed disease activity compared to no intervention.
When early axSpA is defined based on disease duration of <5 years or non-radiographic damage, no differences in response to treatment are found.

Major adverse cardiac event incidence rates at 8 years are low in patients treated with NSAIDs . This study results support the hypothesis of a protective role of NSAIDs and anti-TNF agents in cardiovascular risk in these patients.

A Cochrane review found moderate to high quality evidence for the efficacy of traditional and COX-2 NSAIDs and low to moderate quality evidence for its safety (ie, comparable adverse events with placebo in the short term). No single NSAID appears superior than the rest, and long-term use may decrease radiographic progression of spinal changes.

Recently, the anti-TNFs infliximab and etanercept and golimumab have demonstrated excellent efficacy in ankylosing spondylitis treatment. Anti-TNF therapy has been shown to decrease spine pain and peripheral joint pain and increase function in RCTs. Response is rapid (NNT = 2-3). It is not yet clear if these treatments improve outcomes such as return to work or work productivity.

In multivariable regression without disease activity measures, initiating TNFis compared with NSAIDs was associated with greater improvement in depressive symptoms TNFis have a greater effect than NSAIDs, which is mainly explained by a stronger effect on disease activity..

A Cochrane review found moderate to high quality evidence for the effectiveness of anti-TNF agents in reducing clinical symptoms of ankylosing spondylitis. There were more withdrawals from adverse events, but similar rates of serious adverse events. In the short-term, anti-TNF agents have accetable toxicity. No single agent appears superior.

In one study, the majority of patients receiving the TNF inhibitor remained in employment over 24 months. Anti-TNF therapy reduced absenteeism was reduced from 30% to 6% at 6 months in treated patients. Presenteeism was also reduced from 49% to 28% at 6 months. Otherwork related contexual factors alo played an important role in outcome with treatment with TNF inhibitors.They included but were not limited to, smoking status, quality of contact with colleagues and importance of job for quality of life.
There is no evidence to support use of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs except for the use of sulfasalazine in peripheral joint symptoms.
There are no clinical studies evaluating local steroid injections in peripheral joints; however, expert opinion supports their use.

Peri-operative medication management recommended by ACR and AAHKS guidelines is as follows: (1) DMARDs: continue through surgery, (2) biologic agents/monoclonal antibodies: stop these medications prior to surgery, schedule surgery at the end of the dosing cycle, and resume medications at a minimum of 14 days after surgery in the absence of wound healing problems, (3) severe SLE: continue medications peri-operatively and (4) non-severe SLE discontinue 1 week prior to surgery.
Upadacitinib, a selective JAK1 inhibitor, showed good efficacy and tolerance in a randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial in 62 sites in 20 countries.

COAST-X, a randomized placebo controlled trial at 107 sites worldwide, showed that ixekizumab, a high-affinity interleukin IL-17A monoclonal antibody, was superior to placebo in improving signs and symptoms in patients with non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis. Ixekizumab offers a potential option for patients intolerant to NSAIDs in this subgroup

Prospective cohort studies show pain relief and improvement in function with total hip arthroplasty. In 340 patients with ankylosing spondylitis who had total hip arthroplasty, only 10% needed revision at 10 years. Rates of heterotopic bone formation and re-ankylosing after total hip arthroplasty are not increased.

Spinal surgery is of value in certain patients. Wedge osteotomy may be indicated in patients with severe kyphosis to restore horizontal vision and balance. Cervical fusion may be indicated in patients with segmental instability and pain due to spinal fracture.

Needle-knife combined with eternacept NKCE was shown in randomized controlled trial to reduce hip pain, inflammation, and disease activity and improve hip joint function in AS patients with hip joint involvement.

A review of 11 randomized and quasi-randomized trials with a total of 763 participants showed that group and individual physical therapy leads to significant improvement in relief of symptoms and physical function.
A meta-analysis showed that in the short term, a supervised-exercise program is more effective than home-based exercises at decreasing disease activity in ankylosing spondylitis.

A RCT (n = 502) suggested possible short term benefit of a nurse-led program on self management and self assessment for disease activity in young persons with axial spondyloarthritis in terms of disease activity, exercise and physical activity.
Because of the rapid advances in disease-modifying medications such as the anti-TNFs, once a patient has been diagnosed with definite or probably ankylosing spondylitis, refer to a rheumatologist.
Continuous NSAIDs have been shown to slow radiographic progression of the disease. C
Anti-TNFs may affect disease progression; however, more studies are needed. C

A study found that ankylosing spondylitis patients developed hip fractures earlier and more often compared to a matched cohort. This study suggests that ankylosing spondylitis patients might benefit from more proactive screening, mitigation, and prevention of risk factors for hip fractures. B
Published data describing the natural history of ankylosing spondylitis, disease course, and prognosis are sparse due to a lack of longitudinal prospective studies.

In a prospective study of 51 patients with an average disease duration of 38 years, a predictable pattern over the first 10 years is apparent. Of the patients who had mild spinal restriction after 10 years, 74% did not progress to severe restriction, and 81% of the patients with severe spinal restriction were severely restricted in the first 10 years.

The most serious complication of is spinal fracture. The cervical spine is at increased risk in late disease. Other complications include prostatitis in men, aortic insufficiency, cardiac conduction disturbances, cauda equina syndrome, and pulmonary fibrosis.
A 2-year RCT (N = 215) showed a reduction in radiographic progression in symptomatic patients who were treated with continuous NSAIDs.

Larger studies are needed to prove that anti-TNF treatment inhibits the structural damage of ankylosing spondylitis. A small prospective trial of 41 patients treated with infliximab showed lower radiographic progression compared with 41 controls after 2 years.
A study of certolizumab showed improvement and sustained efficacy in AS and nr-axSpA patients through clinical, patient-reported and QoL outcomes over 4 years.
According to a meta-analysis, prevalence of vertebral fracture is increased in AS as compared to non-AS patients.
In a RCT, Needle Knife combined with Eternacept NKCE showed lower hip pain VAS score, BASDAI score, inflammation , disease activity and improved hip function. NK alone was better than control group.
The assessments in Ankylosing Spondylitis Working Group developed a core data set for use in clinical record keeping.
The core data set includes assessing physical function, pain, spinal mobility, patient's global assessment, stiffness, peripheral joints and entheses, acute phase reactants, fatigue, and imaging.
The American College of Rheumatology has materials for patients to assist them in learning more about the disease and its treatment.
There is insufficient evidence that smoking cessation is effective in preventing the occurence, decreasing symptoms, and improving disease activity of ankylosing spondylitis.

algorithm.title: Diagnostic Algorithm for Approaching the Patient with Ankylosing Spondylitis.

cell.label: 4 of 5 of the following: (1) onset of back discomfort before the age of 40 years, (2) insidious onset, (3) persistence for at least 3 months, (4) associated with morning stiffness, or (5) improvement with exercise?
25% probability of having AS assuming 5% prevalence of AS in chronic low back pain.
Anterior spine flexion of <5 cm (Schober's test) and chest expansion of <2.5 cm increase probability of diagnosis but are often absent in early disease.
Order sacroiliac x-ray. Is the radiologic criterion of grade 2 sacroiilitis bilaterally or grade 3 or 4 unilaterally satisfied?
Patient still has possible early AS. Order HLA-B27.
Patient has a 80% chance of having early AS. Consider a trial of NSAIDs and physical therapy or a rheumatologist referral.
Patient has less than 3% chance of having AS. Consider another diagnosis.
